title: Unemployment and Medical Expense Statements and Relief Extension Months
content:
Patient Services Academy — training note on **Patient Payment Plans**: how the hardship documents a patient has sent to the Patient Financial Assistance Program bear on relief extension months.

## The rule

A patient with an approved award whose assistance file holds an unemployment benefit statement adds 1 relief extension month; a patient with an approved award whose assistance file holds a medical expense statement and no unemployment benefit statement adds 2 relief extension months; any other patient adds none.

Relief extension months are added to the installments still to fall due over which a relief installment spreads the plan's carried balance; months from every source are added together, and the installments with all the relief extension months never carry the plan past its 24th installment.

## What the records must show

- **Approved award** — a case of the patient under the Patient Financial Assistance Program whose status is approved.
- **Assistance file holds a statement** — the patient's assistance file records a document received of that type: an *unemployment benefit statement* or a *medical expense statement*.

| Approved award | Unemployment benefit statement received | Medical expense statement received | Relief extension months |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | No | 1 |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | 1 |
| Yes | No | Yes | 2 |
| Yes | No | No | 0 |
| No | any | any | 0 |

## Questions answered

**The file holds both statements. Which applies?** The unemployment benefit statement: 1 month. The 2-month rule needs a medical expense statement and no unemployment benefit statement.

**The patient sent a medical expense statement, but the application was denied. Any months?** None. Without an approved award, no months are added.

**The file holds two unemployment benefit statements.** Still 1 month; the rule turns on the file holding such a statement, not on how many.
